articles.title: NARC Recommended Groundnut Varieties for Pothwar
articles.author: Dr. Faisal (Researcher)
articles.excerpt: Detailed guide on high-yielding peanut varieties suited for rainfed conditions of the Pothwar region including BARI-2016.
articles.content: The Pothwar region accounts for the majority of groundnut production in Pakistan. The National Agricultural Research Centre (NARC) highly recommends the BARI-2016 variety due to its high yield potential and resistance to drought conditions. Farmers are advised to maintain a seed rate of 25-30 kg per acre and ensure sowing between April and May. Proper land preparation, including deep ploughing and planking, is crucial for moisture conservation.

articles.title: Early Leaf Spot (Cercospora arachidicola) Management Protocol
articles.author: BARI Chakwal
articles.excerpt: Preventive measures and fungicidal recommendations for controlling Early Leaf Spot in peanut crops during monsoon season.
articles.content: Early Leaf Spot is a devastating fungal disease that thrives in high humidity (>80%) and temperatures between 25-30°C. Initial symptoms include brown circular spots surrounded by yellow halos on the upper leaf surface. Management protocols dictate prophylactic spraying of systemic fungicides such as Chlorothalonil (2ml/L) immediately upon symptom onset. Cultural practices like crop rotation and deep burying of crop residues significantly reduce primary inoculum.

articles.title: Seed Viability and Germination Testing Guidelines
articles.author: Agricultural Extension Dept
articles.excerpt: Standard procedures for testing peanut seed germination rates before sowing to ensure optimal plant density.
articles.content: To achieve optimal plant density (approx. 60,000 plants/acre), seed viability testing must be conducted 2 weeks prior to sowing. Select 100 random seeds from the batch. Soak them overnight and place them in moist paper towels at room temperature. A germination rate of >85% within 7 days is considered standard for certified seeds. Treat seeds with Imidacloprid and Thiram before planting to prevent soil-borne pests and seedling rot.

articles.title: Historical Outbreak Analysis: Pothwar Region 2022-2025
articles.author: Crop Reporting Service
articles.excerpt: A retrospective analysis of the severe Rosette Virus and Late Leaf Spot outbreaks and their economic impact.
articles.content: Between 2022 and 2025, the Pothwar region experienced unusually heavy late-monsoon showers, triggering widespread outbreaks of Late Leaf Spot and Groundnut Rosette Virus (GRV). GRV, transmitted by the aphid Aphis craccivora, caused up to 40% yield loss in late-sown fields. Data analysis reveals that fields planted early (mid-April) experienced significantly lower vector pressure, highlighting the importance of adjusting planting windows in response to changing climatic patterns.

articles.title: Predictive Modeling for Fungal Pathogen Spores
articles.author: Agri-Tech AI Lab
articles.excerpt: Using micro-climate data to predict the dispersion of fungal spores for precision fungicide application.
articles.content: Our latest predictive models integrate real-time field telemetry (temperature, leaf wetness duration, and relative humidity) to forecast spore germination events. We found that 12 consecutive hours of leaf wetness combined with temperatures above 22°C triggers massive spore release. By applying protective fungicides exactly 48 hours prior to these predicted events, farmers can reduce chemical usage by 30% while maintaining complete crop protection.

aiResponses.disease: Based on BARI's Disease Management Protocol, Early Leaf Spot loves high humidity. You should spray a fungicide like Chlorothalonil (2ml per Litre of water) as soon as you see brown spots with yellow rings. Also, remember to clear out old plant debris from your field to stop the fungus from surviving the winter.
aiResponses.seed: According to NARC and Extension guidelines, you should use the BARI-2016 variety. Use 25-30 kg of seeds per acre and sow between April and May. Before planting, test your seeds by sprouting 100 of them in wet paper towels—if 85 sprout, you're good to go! Don't forget to treat them with fungicide before putting them in the soil.
aiResponses.general: I couldn't find specific institutional research for that exact query. However, generally, ensuring good drainage, timely weeding, and using certified NARC/BARI seed varieties will protect your yield. Try asking about 'leaf spot', 'seeds', or 'sowing times'.

dashboard.article1Title: NARC Recommended Groundnut Varieties for Pothwar
dashboard.article2Title: Managing Collar Rot in Rainfed Areas
dashboard.article1Summary: Detailed guide on high-yielding peanut varieties suited for rainfed conditions of the Pothwar region including BARI-2016.
dashboard.article2Summary: Essential preventative and responsive measures for combating Aspergillus niger infections in peanut crops.
dashboard.article3Summary: A comprehensive guide on determining the right time to harvest to maximize both yield and oil content.
dashboard.article4Summary: Techniques for retaining soil moisture during dry spells in the rainfed Pothwar region.
dashboard.article1Content: The Pothwar region accounts for the majority of groundnut production in Pakistan. The National Agricultural Research Centre (NARC) highly recommends the BARI-2016 variety due to its high yield potential and resistance to drought conditions. Farmers are advised to maintain a seed rate of 25-30 kg per acre and ensure sowing between April and May. Proper land preparation, including deep ploughing and planking, is crucial for moisture conservation.
dashboard.article2Content: Collar rot, caused by Aspergillus niger, remains a significant threat in the Chakwal and Attock districts. Symptoms appear as sudden wilting of branches followed by plant death. Preventative measures include treating seeds with recommended fungicides before sowing and avoiding deep planting. Maintaining proper field drainage during the monsoon is critical.
dashboard.article3Content: Determining the correct harvest time is crucial for maximizing yield and oil content. Harvest when 70-80% of the pods show dark maturity inside the shell. Delaying harvest can lead to pod shedding in the soil, while early harvesting reduces quality. After digging, allow the plants to dry in the field for 2-3 days before threshing to reduce moisture to a safe 8-10% level.
dashboard.article4Content: In the rainfed Pothwar region, conserving soil moisture is the key to a successful peanut crop. Deep summer ploughing helps harvest rainwater. Following the first monsoon showers, immediate sowing is recommended. Regular weeding during the first 45 days reduces competition for moisture. Applying a mulch layer can further prevent evaporation during dry spells.
